title: Pistachio macaron
subtitle: Pale green shells filled with pistachio buttercream or praline cream
excerpt: French macaron shells with a small portion of finely ground pistachio replacing some of the almond flour, giving a subtle green tint and a nuttier flavour. Filled with a pistachio buttercream or a white chocolate ganache laced with pistachio paste. More delicate than a plain almond shell.
sourceNotes: Pistachio macarons are a standard French patisserie variety. The partial pistachio flour substitution in the shell is a common technique to achieve natural colour and flavour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled macarons in a single layer, then box. Defrost for 1 hour at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shells keep in an airtight tin for 2 days unfilled. Fill on the day or day before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: The folding technique for macaron batter: deflating the meringue into the dry ingredients until the batter flows in a slow, thick ribbon. Under-folding produces domed cracked shells; over-folding produces flat thin ones.

content.text: Pistachio macarons use a partial pistachio substitution in the shell, replacing 40 g of the ground almonds with finely blitzed unsalted pistachios. This gives the shell a pale green tint and a rounder, nuttier flavour without using artificial colouring. The
technique is identical to a plain macaron shell.

attrs.prepNote: blitzed to a fine powder and sifted
aged at room temperature for 24 hours (about 4 medium eggs)
blitzed to a paste with a little oil, for the filling

content.text: Prepare the pistachio powder: blitz 40 g unsalted pistachios in a food processor until fine. Sift and discard any large pieces. Combine with the ground almonds and icing sugar.

Make an Italian meringue: cook 150 g caster sugar with 45 ml water to 118°C (soft-ball stage, 115 to 120°C). Whisk 55 g aged egg whites to soft peaks. Pour the hot syrup in a thin stream into the whites while whisking. Whisk until stiff, glossy, and at room temperature.

Mix the almond-pistachio-icing sugar powder with the remaining 55 g egg whites to a rough paste. Fold the meringue in three additions. The batter is ready when it flows in a slow ribbon from the spatula. Pipe 3.5 cm rounds on parchment-lined trays. Bang the trays on the bench to release bubbles. Rest 45 to 60 minutes until a skin forms. Bake at 150°C (conventional) for 14 to 15 minutes.

Blitz 40 g pistachios in a food processor with a small amount of neutral oil until a paste forms. Beat 150 g softened butter with 100 g icing sugar until pale. Fold in the pistachio paste. Pipe a small mound onto the flat side of one cold shell and sandwich with another.
